title: Hannibal: invasion and return
hook: Did crossing the Alps settle the war?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: An invasion route is not the whole war.

claims.text: 218 BCE: From Iberia. Hannibal’s army leaves Iberia for Italy.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Second Punic War paragraphs and Zama (202 BCE)

claims.text: 218 BCE: Alpine crossing. The army crosses the Alps.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Second Punic War paragraphs and Zama (202 BCE)

claims.text: 218–201 BCE: Italian campaign. Many Roman allies remain with Rome.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Second Punic War paragraphs and Zama (202 BCE)

claims.text: 202 BCE: Return to Africa. Rome wins at Zama in North Africa.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Second Punic War paragraphs and Zama (202 BCE)

claims.text: An invasion route is not the whole war. Crossing the Alps brought Hannibal’s army into Italy, but many Roman allies stayed with Rome. A Roman campaign in Africa drew Hannibal back; Rome’s victory at Zama ended the contest on another shore.
claims.source: https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/6-4-the-roman-republic — Second Punic War paragraphs and Zama (202 BCE)

claims.text: The Alpine pass and exact march are uncertain; this line does not choose a pass.
